acceptance_criteria: Dedicated codex/0.2-app-sdk-contract branch and isolated worktree.
DF-01 state, ownership, dependency, activation-gate, resume, and verification model is followed; shared-file proposals are flagged for integration-owner checkpoint.
App manifest v1 schema and host loader cover identity, publisher, entrypoint, locales, resources, intents, requested capabilities, optional services, and state compatibility.
App identity remains stable and independent from display names, locale, filesystem location, and execution identity.
Host-side app registration rejects duplicate identifiers and numeric AppId collisions; a fixture registers before launch.
Lifecycle state and events are distinct; invalid transitions and abnormal termination are represented.
State backend contract covers app namespace, versions, load/save/reset, missing/corrupt data, and migrations.
Intent and deep-link contract validates declarations, payload metadata, source/target and correlation identity.
Transport-independent IPC v1 envelope supports request/response/event/error, correlation and request IDs, ordering metadata, and unsupported-version errors.
Common error model and capability handoff boundary do not duplicate policy or grant authority.
Localization handles en-US and ja-JP as first-class locales with en-US fallback and unknown-locale behavior.
Manifest schema, SDK contract, IPC protocol, and persisted-state versions are independent and documented.
At least three SDK-owned first-party-like fixtures pass manifest, unit, and integration coverage.
Schema validation, focused fmt, Clippy, tests, relevant package regression tests, and ./nagi dev verify pass.
App SDK architecture, runtime adapter points, and first-party adoption guidance are documented.
No runtime app-host integration, M17/M18-M30 change, first-party app change, Capability implementation, or Wayback implementation.
Workstream state and handoff reflect actual evidence; final commit is pushed and worktree is clean.
deferred: Runtime app-host binding, lifecycle delivery, and process execution until M30 PASS and explicit 0.2 integration checkpoint.
Concrete IPC transport, persistent filesystem/VFS backend, Capability policy engine, and compositor/window surface integration remain owned by their respective runtime/platform workstreams.
Migration of the existing M16 package parser and adoption by real first-party apps require a later compatibility/integration checkpoint.
